title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant & Payroll Coordinator

Location: Durham
Salary: £35,000+ DOE
Hours: 37.5 hours per week (Monday to Friday)
Working Hours: 8:00am-4:00pm, 8:30am-4:30pm, or 9:00am-5:00pm
Holiday: 25 days plus bank holidays (7 days reserved for Christmas shutdown)

My client is a successful and rapidly growing business that has recently expanded its operations with multiple new offices. They are looking to recruit a proactive and driven Accounts Assistant & Payroll Coordinator who can take ownership of key finance processes and play an important role in supporting the continued growth of the business.

This is a varied, hands-on position that will combine accounting, payroll and CIS responsibilities, while also providing the opportunity to become involved in month-end processes, VAT submissions and ongoing improvements across the finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Process weekly/monthly payroll, ensuring all payroll data is accurate and submitted within agreed deadlines.
- Post and allocate bank transactions, maintaining accurate financial records across the finance systems.
- Process, review and validate supplier invoices, ensuring all costs are correctly coded and authorised.
- Process subcontractor invoices and maintain accurate CIS records.
- Prepare supplier payment runs and subcontractor payment schedules for approval and payment.
- Review employee expense claims, checking receipts and supporting documentation, maintaining expense records within Excel and preparing payment lists.
- Process employee expenses within Sage.
- Complete CIS reconciliations and ensure compliance with relevant regulations.
- Respond to payroll, supplier and subcontractor queries in a timely manner.
- Produce and maintain reports using Excel to support finance operations and decision-making.
- Support the development and improvement of finance processes, systems and reporting capabilities.
- Build strong working relationships with site teams and operational departments to ensure the smooth flow of payroll and expense information.
- Provide support and guidance to a junior member of the accounts team.

Month-End Responsibilities
- Complete bank reconciliations and investigate any outstanding variances.
- Perform payroll reconciliations to ensure accuracy between payroll and financial records.
- Post job costing and overhead allocations, including:
- Company vans
- Company cars
- Fuel costs
- Assist with the preparation of month-end accounts and management reporting.
- Support VAT return preparation and submissions.
- Produce travel expense analysis for Head Office.
- Reconcile supplier statements and investigate any discrepancies.
- Assist in maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring month-end deadlines are achieved.

About You
- Has experience within accounts and payroll
- Has CIS knowledge and experience
- Is confident using Excel and accounting systems such as Sage
- Can work independently and take ownership of processes

The Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity to join a business during an exciting period of growth. The role offers genuine responsibility, exposure to a broad range of finance activities and the chance to make a real impact on the development of the finance function while working as part of a close-knit and supportive team.

If you're interested, please submit your CV now!

title: Accounts Payable Assistant
description:

This is a business-critical role responsible for ensuring the accurate and timely processing of supplier invoices and payments, maintaining strong supplier relationships, and supporting month-end finance activities. The successful candidate will play an integral role in ensuring the smooth running of the purchase ledger function while supporting reporting deadlines and prompt payment performance.

What's in it for you?
- Hybrid working with up to 3 days per week from home
- Flexible working hours with core hours of 8:00am - 4:00pm
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Holiday buy and sell scheme
- Complimentary onsite breakfast, tea and coffee
- Regular team social events and company celebrations
- Relaxed and casual dress code
- Dedicated wellbeing and mental health support
- Modern, collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to join a growing business with genuine career progression opportunities

What will you be doing?
- Accurately processing high volumes of supplier invoices through the company's invoice management system
- Ensuring invoices are correctly coded, authorised and posted within agreed deadlines
- Investigating and resolving invoice discrepancies with suppliers and internal stakeholders
- Managing Accounts Payable queries and maintaining prompt responses to supplier enquiries
- Preparing payment runs and ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time
- Monitoring payment schedules and proactively escalating any potential delays or risks
- Supporting the achievement and continuous improvement of prompt payment performance targets

- Building strong relationships with suppliers and colleagues across the wider business
- Collaborating with Finance and operational teams to ensure efficient processing and payment of supplier invoices

Who you need to be

This role is best suited for someone with experience working in a similar Account Payable or Purchaser Ledger position, with strong invoice processing and reconciliation experience. You must have excellent attention to detail, with stroong organisation and communication skills. Experience of Payroll would be advantageous.

If this sounds like you, what are you waiting for, apply today!

title: Accounts Payable Assistant
description:
Job Description:

Are you an experienced Accounts Payable professional looking for your next opportunity? We are supporting a client in the search for a detail-oriented Accounts Payable Assistant to join their finance team in Stockton-on-Tees.

As part of a well-established and growing organisation, you'll play a key role in ensuring the smooth running of the purchase ledger function, maintaining strong supplier relationships, and supporting month-end finance activities.

Salary: £29,000 - £30,000

Hours: 42.5 hours per week, office based

Job Type: Full-time

Role Summary

We are looking for an Accounts Payable Assistant. The role will involve managing supplier relationships, planning supplier payments, maintaining accurate cashflow information and supporting the wider finance function with banking, reconciliations and spend analysis.

Key Responsibilities

Supplier Payments & Relationships
- Liaise with suppliers and build strong working relationships.
- Respond to and resolve supplier queries.
- Liaise with suppliers regarding outstanding balances and payment plans.
- Create and plan regular supplier payment runs.
- Input supplier payments and Direct Debits into the cashflow forecasting spreadsheet.
- Work closely with the Accounts Receivable team to maintain an accurate view of upcoming cash movements.
- Process Overhead invoices direct to our Sage 50 accounts system

Banking & Reconciliation
- Daily posting of bank payments onto Sage 50 Accounts.
- Reconcile company bank accounts (shared responsibility)
- Investigate and resolve any discrepancies.
- Ensure banking payment transactions are accurately recorded and up to date.
- Keeping the AP ledger 'clean' and making sure no payments on account/debit balances are showing without reason.

Accounts Inbox
- Monitor the Accounts & statements inboxes on a daily basis (shared responsibility)
- Distribute emails to the relevant person or department.
- Resolve queries where appropriate and follow up on outstanding items.
- Deal with supplier and finance-related correspondence promptly.

Spend Analysis
- Post and analyse credit card transactions. (Monthly)
- Carry out analysis to identify spending patterns and areas of expenditure.
- Post and analyse fuel card transactions (Bi-Weekly)
- Identify trends or unusual expenditure and report findings where appropriate.
- Complete ad hoc financial analysis and duties as required.

About You

We are looking for someone who is organised, commercially aware and confident dealing with suppliers and financial information.

You will have:
- Previous experience of managing/owning an Accounts Payable function in a busy fast-paced environment
- Good understanding of accounting processes and bank reconciliations.
- Experience using Sage 50 Accounts.
- Basic Excel skills.
- Strong attention to detail.
- Good communication skills and confident in dealing with suppliers.
- The ability to investigate and resolve queries.
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage your own workload.
- A proactive approach to problem solving.
- The ability to analyse financial information and identify trends.
- Good understanding of how supplier payments and cashflow impact the business.
- Experience working in, or the ability to adapt to, a fast-paced and growing business.
- Ability to work well within a small accounts team.

Benefits:
- Life insurance
- On-site parking
- Private medical insurance

Work Location: In person

title: Credit Control
description:
The Company
Ready for a Credit Control role that gives you more ownership, variety and room to develop and join a supportive finance team where you can make a visible contribution.

We're recruiting for a well-established finance team seeking a Credit Controller to manage a varied portfolio across three legal entities. It's a varied position where you'll have the opportunity to strengthen your experience across credit control, account reconciliation, credit risk and the wider ledger function.

The Role
As the Credit Controller you will report into the Credit Control & Purchase Ledger Manager, responsible for:
- Managing customer accounts from collection through to query resolution

- Reviewing aged debt and escalating higher-risk accounts
- Reconciling accounts and investigating discrepancies
- Resolving disputed invoices
- Monitoring credit limits and payment patterns

This could work equally well for someone looking to develop their career or an experienced Credit Controller who can make an immediate contribution.

What's on Offer

- Pension
- Death in Service
- Employee purchase scheme
- Employee Assistance Programme
- AAT study support

Interested? Apply now for a confidential conversation.

title: Finance Assistant
company: Penn Gregory Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Great opportunity for an experienced Finance Assistant to join a fast growing organisation. Standard hours are 8am - 4pm, however there is flexibility for the right person to reduce slightly to fit into personal schedules. Career progression definitely an option!

Job Purpose

The Finance Assistant supports the Accounts team across a broad range of finance functions, including accounts payable, cash and bank. A key part of the role is learning the accounts receivable process, including our invoice discounting facility, so that you can support it day to day and provide cover when needed.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable
- Process supplier invoices accurately and promptly, matching them to purchase orders and delivery records and resolving any discrepancies with suppliers and site teams.
- Reconcile supplier statements and respond to supplier queries.
- Prepare supplier payment runs for approval in line with agreed payment terms.

Cash and Bank
- Post daily bank transactions, including receipts, payments and direct debits, to the accounts system.
- Complete regular bank reconciliations and investigate any unreconciled items.
- Maintain cash records and help prepare cash flow forecasts.
- Process and reconcile company credit card transactions and expense claims.

Accounts Receivable
- Learn the full accounts receivable process so you can support the role day to day and provide cover during holidays and absences.
- Raise customer invoices and credit notes in line with agreed pricing and completed works.
- Allocate customer receipts and maintain accurate customer accounts.
- Assist with credit control, including reviewing aged debt and chasing overdue payments.
- Learn to operate the company's invoice discounting facility, including uploading sales ledger information, reconciling the facility account and requesting funding drawdowns.

General Administration
- Handle finance-related telephone and email enquiries and maintain organised filing systems.
- Provide general support to the Accounts team and the wider business.

Skills and Experience

Essential
- Previous experience in a finance or accounts role, including accounts payable and bank reconciliations.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook.
- Strong numerical skills and close attention to detail.
- Good communication skills and the ability to manage a varied workload to deadlines.

Desirable
- Experience of accounts receivable or credit control.
- Experience of invoice discounting or invoice finance.
- Experience in the environmental, waste management, construction or industrial services sector.
- Experience with accounts software (e.g. Sage, Xero or similar).

Personal Attributes
- Organised, methodical and proactive, with a willingness to learn new skills.
- Confident liaising with colleagues, customers and suppliers.
- Able to work independently and as part of a team.
- Discreet when handling confidential financial information.

title: Payroll Clerk
company: Baltic Recruitment Services Ltd - Agency - Temporary
description:
Baltic Recruitment are currently recruiting for a Payroll Clerk for a client located in Darlington. Our client is looking to appoint an experienced Payroll Clerk to join their team on an interim basis while they undertake recruitment for a permanent appointment.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced payroll professional with a strong background in education payroll to join a busy and rewarding working environment. The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting and managing the end-to-end payroll process, ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time, whilst maintaining compliance with relevant payroll legislation and procedures.

This is an office based role with flexibility to work from home. Preferably 4-days in the office and 1 day working from home. Although initially an interim position, there is potential for the role to become permanent for the right candidate.

Payroll Clerk Main Duties and Responsibilities:
- Manage and process the full end-to-end payroll function for employees across the Trust.
- Process monthly payroll accurately and within agreed deadlines.
- Calculate and process new starters, leavers, salary changes, contractual amendments and other employee adjustments.
- Administer statutory payments, including SSP, SMP, SPP and other relevant statutory entitlements.
- Process overtime, additional hours, deductions, allowances and absence-related payments.
- Ensure payroll information is accurate and up to date, maintaining employee records and payroll documentation.
- Reconcile payroll data and investigate and resolve any discrepancies.
- Respond to payroll-related queries from employees and managers, providing a professional and confidential service.
- Liaise with HR and other departments to ensure payroll information is received and processed correctly.
- Ensure compliance with HMRC requirements, pension regulations and relevant payroll legislation.
- Maintain strict confidentiality when handling sensitive employee and financial information.

Payroll Clerk Applicants:

Essential Requirements
- Proven experience managing end-to-end payroll within an education environment.
- Strong understanding of payroll processes, procedures and statutory requirements.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Ability to work to strict deadlines within a busy payroll environment.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.
- Ability to handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion.

Desirable Requirements
- Previous experience using the Edupay payroll system is highly desirable.
- Experience processing payroll for a Multi-Academy Trust.

Working Monday - Thursday, 8:00am - 4:00pm and Friday, 8:00am - 3:30pm. Hourly rate is: 17.17 - 18.44 per hour (depending on experience). Although initially an interim position, there is potential for the role to become permanent for the right candidate.

- Qualified by experience or AAT Qualified
- Conscientious team player
- Enthusiastic
- Willing to learn
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills
- A proactive and solutions-focused approach
- A commitment to delivering excellent client service

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who shares our values, enjoys working collaboratively and is passionate about delivering great results.

At TC Group you'll find:

- Opportunities for career progression within a fast-growing business

title: Credit Control
description:
Credit Controller

Newcastle upon Tyne £36,000 - £39,500 per year Permanent

Consula is recruiting on behalf of a growing professional services group with its northern hub in Newcastle upon Tyne for an organised and confident Credit Controller.

Our client has built a strong reputation for reliable service and long-standing customer relationships, and as the business continues to grow, they are strengthening their finance team with a credit control specialist who can protect cash flow while keeping customers on side.

In this role, you will own a ledger serving corporate and public sector clients across the North East and Scotland. You will be the friendly, persistent voice that keeps accounts up to date, resolving queries quickly and making sure payments arrive on time. Your work has a direct impact on the business's cash position, its customer relationships and the accuracy of month-end reporting.

The office sits close to Newcastle Central Station and the Metro, making it an easy daily commute from across Tyneside, Northumberland and County Durham.

Location: Newcastle

Salary: £36,000 - £39,500 per year

Employment: Permanent

THE ROLE

As Credit Controller, you will manage the full collections cycle for your ledger, working closely with sales, customer service and the wider finance team.
- Managing a designated sales ledger, chasing overdue balances by telephone and email in a professional, solution-focused way.
- Prioritising collections activity using aged debt reports to reduce debtor days and keep overdue balances under control.
- Investigating and resolving invoice queries, disputes and pricing discrepancies with internal teams.
- Setting up and monitoring payment plans, and escalating persistent non-payment in line with credit policy.
- Allocating cash receipts and reconciling customer accounts accurately and promptly.
- Carrying out credit checks on new and existing customers and recommending appropriate credit limits.
- Placing accounts on stop where required and communicating clearly with account managers.
- Preparing weekly cash forecasts and aged debt reports for the Finance Manager.
- Supporting month-end close, audit requests and continuous improvement of the credit control process.

ABOUT YOU

Our client is keen to meet people who are calm under pressure, persuasive on the phone and meticulous with detail.

Essential:
- Proven experience in credit control, collections or accounts receivable.
- Confident, courteous telephone manner with the resilience to handle difficult conversations.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a high volume of accounts at once.
- Good working knowledge of Excel, including filters, lookups and pivot tables.
- High standards of accuracy when allocating cash and reconciling accounts.

Desirable:
- Experience of accounting systems such as Sage, Xero, SAP, Dynamics or similar.
- Understanding of credit checking tools and the debt recovery process.
- AAT or CICM qualification, or working towards one.

A TYPICAL DAY

You will start the morning by reviewing yesterday's receipts, allocating cash and checking which accounts are now due or overdue. Mid-morning is focused on your call list, speaking with customers, agreeing payment dates and logging every conversation. In the afternoon you will chase up outstanding queries with colleagues in sales and operations, review credit applications and update your aged debt report, finishing the day with a clear plan of priorities for tomorrow.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT
- A secure, permanent role within an established and supportive Newcastle finance team.
- 28 days' annual leave including bank holidays.
- Workplace pension scheme with employer contributions.
- Study support towards AAT or CICM qualifications for the right person.
- Structured induction and clear progression routes within the finance function.
- A friendly team culture with regular recognition of good work.
- Health and wellbeing support, including an employee assistance programme.

If you are a determined, organised credit control professional looking for your next step, we would be delighted to hear from you. Apply through Consula today and Doug, our AI talent partner, will be in touch to discuss the role further.
